description: Helm charts and container images only. Terraform providers, the pinned Talos/Kubernetes versions and the Python deps are deliberately left alone: a provider bump can rewrite infrastructure, and a Talos upgrade is a node reboot that no bot should start.

packageRules.description: Patch and minor bumps merge themselves once CI is green. The checks that gate this are the same ones a human would look at, and leaving them queued for review is how a homelab ends up a year behind.
Majors always get a PR. They carry migrations, renamed values and removed APIs — the cases where reading the changelog is the whole job.

Gitea holds the repo Flux reconciles from, Flux applies it, and the runner and Renovate drive the loop. An unattended bump to any of them can lock you out of your own GitOps loop, so all are review-only whatever the semver says.

Never propose a major bump for a stateful datastore. Postgres refuses to start on a data directory written by an older major, so this is a pg_upgrade or dump-restore migration, not a tag change — and a PR that reads as routine is one click from taking Immich, Outline and AdventureLog down. Minor and patch still flow.

Flux is upgraded as a bundle, never a tag at a time. gotk-components.yaml is generated by `flux install --export` and carries the CRDs alongside all four controllers for one release; bumping a single image leaves that controller newer than the CRDs it reads and than its three siblings. Upgrade with the flux CLI and regenerate the file.
